criteria.label: PARITY
similar: Matching isometric projection, yaw, pitch, and terrain axes.
Plants, city, river, and industrial district occupy the same world-frame positions.
different: The CANDIDATE bottom navigation masks a narrow lower-center portion of the otherwise matching frame.

evidence.observation: Full map shows the shared diagonal mountain-to-city framing and elevated isometric viewpoint.
Visible world uses the same projection, viewpoint, and landmark placement.
Lower-center world remains exposed to the frame edge.

criteria.label: PARITY
similar: City, central industry, roads, and transmission corridors have matching occupied footprints.
Sparse mountain and valley regions balance the dense lower and right-side districts identically.
different: Darker CANDIDATE contrast makes small terrain and building marks read slightly busier without changing mass distribution.

evidence.observation: Central industrial mass, lower infrastructure, and right city edge establish the same density pattern.
Industrial blocks, roads, and city mass align with the reference footprint.
The right-side city has the same compact building concentration.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: The channel follows the same winding mountain-to-industrial curvature.
Bank depth and the lower bridge attachment occur at matching locations.
different: CANDIDATE water and banks are darker and higher-contrast, with less pale reflective lift.

evidence.observation: Pale winding channel descends through the valley and meets the bridge near the industrial district.
Channel geometry and bridge junction match, while water and banks render darker.

criteria.label: PARITY
similar: Plants A and B retain matching sizes relative to mountains, city blocks, and distance arcs.
Transmission towers and the lower substation preserve the same relative silhouette scale.
different: CANDIDATE's sharper outlines make some tower silhouettes read marginally thinner, not differently sized.

evidence.observation: Both nuclear plant silhouettes have the same relative scale and placement.
Plant footprints and dome/cooling-tower proportions match the reference.
Towers and substation share the same scale relationship with the industrial buildings.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use blackened riveted metal, muted concrete, brown soil, and amber practical lighting.
Terrain, structures, and chrome overlays share the same weathered industrial cohesion.
different: CANDIDATE has deeper blacks, sharper texture, and stronger amber saturation; REFERENCE is softer and slightly grayer.

evidence.observation: Soft gray-brown terrain and concrete sit beneath restrained amber lighting.
The same material family is rendered with darker midtones and crisper texture.
Inspector uses layered, worn black metal with amber and cyan edging.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Amber routes connect both plant sites with the same tower spacing and attachment geometry.
Cyan energized lines follow the same lower route through towers and the substation.
different: CANDIDATE conductors and voltage plaques are slightly crisper and brighter, with different glyph formatting.

evidence.observation: Amber plant corridors, pylons, and route labels follow the shared geometry.
Amber corridors attach to the same plants and towers with matching readability.
Cyan lower network traces the same energized route and substation attachment.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Top status bar, left technology rail, and right inspector share the same industrial chrome system.
Inspector cards preserve matching amber/cyan hierarchy, totals, dividers, and stacked action buttons.
different: CANDIDATE adds a large four-tab bottom navigation strip absent from REFERENCE, materially increasing overlay footprint.
English and Korean glyph systems produce visibly different label widths and text texture.

evidence.observation: Top status chrome and left icon rail establish the shared industrial HUD language.
Matching chrome, icon order, and status hierarchy appear with Korean glyphs.
Right inspector has two framed comparison cards and two stacked action controls.
